walkthroughs.name: Why there is one door and one queue

beats.heading: Two callers, one operation
beats.body: A pane's command and a voice tool call arrive from opposite directions and become the same four operations. Nothing reaches a workhorse another way, so admission, settlement and reporting have one place to live.

beats.heading: One turn at a time
beats.body: The queue holds the submissions for one thread and starts one. A thread running two turns would interleave their edits to the same repository, and neither would be reproducible.

beats.heading: A start is a staged operation
beats.body: Opening a thread is staged in the epoch ledger before it is sent and committed after. A child that dies mid-flight leaves an operation whose outcome is stated as unknown rather than a binding nobody can account for.

beats.heading: A wait cannot close a cycle
beats.body: Every waiting tool registers its edge, so a thread waiting on something that is waiting on it is refused instead of hanging until a timeout nobody set.
